title: Restocking Merchandise
text: “Hmm... seems like it hurts less if I do it, so let’s hold off.”
“Understood!”
I was going to give the pressure point one jab with my maximum firepower, but decided against it.
“I was thinking I could loosen up those stiff muscles of yours in an instant and turn them into octopus-tender mush, I say.”
“That’s going to end badly if you overdo it. Anyway, for now, Teo, just lie down in the carriage with the needles and moxa still in.”
After giving that order, Father next approached the mixed-breed lizardman known as Sion.
Father and the mixed-breed lizardman stared at each other in silence. I could tell he was on guard.
“Teo and Wolf aren’t at a usable level yet. Sion, once we get off the carriage, can I count on you to assist me?”
“...Understood.”

The mixed-breed lizardman nodded, as if to say he’d obey within the bounds of orders. According to Father, he laughed wryly afterward, saying he couldn’t expect to earn trust right away. But Father would come to be adored by his slaves, I say. He’d end up being adored fairly quickly, though—how would that go, I wonder? Father stared intently at the mixed-breed lizardman.
The mixed-breed lizardman quickly averted his gaze.
“You too...”
“Hm?”
“Do you also think I’m strange?”
“About what?”
At the mixed-breed lizardman’s question, Father tilted his head slightly.
But the mixed-breed lizardman didn’t answer Father’s question.
“...Sion, I don’t know you well enough to know what you’re ashamed of. But do you think it’s something to be ashamed of?”
The mixed-breed lizardman scowled.
“That face says you don’t think so. Then don’t go out of your way to twist the knife in your own wound. The opinions and rumors of people you barely know are... worth less than garbage.”

Father had once been falsely accused by the Crimson Swine, after all. That’s precisely why he must have had feelings about bad reputations. Well, I tried imagining what kind of worries the mixed-breed lizardman might be carrying. Judging from the way he put it, I’d guess it has something to do with being a half-breed? Father probably guessed as much too. He really does have sharp instincts sometimes, much like Filo-tan. Big Sister too, I say. And so the carriage moved on, quietly yet swiftly. A carriage pulled by a Filolial-sama moves faster than an ordinary carriage.
“Heheh, you there, caravan! Halt!”
“Oi! Hand over your cargo nice and quiet, and we won’t take your lives!”
“In the name of God, we’ll deal righteous punishment upon you devils!”
“Bwoink!”
So said this bunch, oddly suspicious even for bandits, who blocked our path as we traveled.
“Waaah...”
“When it’s this blatant, it’s impossible not to see through it.”

The Siltvelt envoy leapt over from another carriage to ours, coming to ask Father for instructions. No doubt they were Three Heroes Church followers. In this loop, I too had been attacked by a fake hero at the guild. Of course, I planned to keep earning through the guild too. If I earn too much I’ll get marked, though... somewhere around Zeltoble would probably be best for that.
“Heheh, Father, resources have come waltzing right up to us. A capture opportunity, I say, uheeheehee.”
“You don’t need to copy them! You don’t need to sink to their level! Anyway, back to the topic... you’re treating bandits like resources?”
“Indeed I am. Shall I exploit them using Father’s own personally-taught method, then release them?”
“Wait, hold on... is that about some other loop’s version of me?”
Father said this with a look of exasperation for some reason.
“Now that I think about it, there was that thing about slaves too... just what version of me do you actually know, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Bandit-release is the method used by the Fathers who couldn’t save people from false accusations, I say.”
Father put a hand to his head. What’s the matter, I wonder?
“My heart aches for the hardships and changes of the possible Shield Hero-sama that Spear Hero-sama has come to know.”
“Well... still, right now I’m a slave trader’s apprentice... I suppose I should handle this appropriately.”
“Bark?”

Wolf stood ready, as if asking, Work? Dispose of them? Should he dispose of them? He seemed remarkably calm—no doubt he was used to fighting this sort of scum. You could say it suited a battle slave well.
“Wolf, there’s no need for you to fight here, of all places.”
Father gave a wry smile as he stroked Wolf’s face.
“Whimper?”
“Oi! Get your asses out here already!”
So shouted the bandits (Three Heroes Church followers), letting an arrow fly.
“Air Strike Shield.”
Before Filolial-sama could intercept the arrow that came flying, Father put up a shield and stopped it.
“No time left to talk, it seems.”
“Then shall I take care of this quickly?”
“Don’t kill them, okay?”
“Of course not—this is restocking merchandise, after all!”
Bandits don’t need human rights, I say!
“No, that’s not really what I meant, but...”
“Then here I go! Aiming Lancer IV, I say!”
To boost the lock count, I unleashed Aiming Lancer at level IV, blasting it at every last one of the bandits.
“Wha—GYAAAAAAAAAAH!?”
“Th-the spear’s flying on some weird trajectory—waaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
“BWOIIIIIINK!?”
“—and then, Paralyze Lance V, I say!”
So, while they were sent flying and left unable to move, I swiftly hopped down from the carriage and followed up by inflicting a status ailment.
“Merchandise acquired, I say!”
“It’s Dark Hunt <Guaranteed Capture>!”
“There it is, there it is, amazing~!”
“They’re all zappy and twitchy~!”
Yeah! I say! Filolial-sama’s cheering feels absolutely wonderful.
“You’re acting like this is some monster-catching game...”
Father said, scratching his head.
“Foolish people, aren’t they. Disguising themselves as bandits to attack us... What shall we do? If we let them go now, they might well spread false rumors about us.”
The Siltvelt envoy, seemingly growing accustomed to all this, asked Father.
“Fortunately, this caravan is also here to purchase slaves. So we can impose a fitting punishment on bandits who picked the wrong carriage to attack.”
“You’re getting pretty into this after all.”
“When in Rome, as they say, it seems important to follow local customs, so I’ll assist Shield Hero-sama’s decisions as best I can.”
At the Siltvelt envoy’s words, Father let out a sigh. Was that no good, I wonder?
“In this case, I think it best to use Spear Hero-sama’s means of transport to carry them out of Melromarc, and sell them off as slaves there. Preferably somewhere it can’t be traced back to us.”
“I think it’s probably the best option, but the method’s pretty brutal...”
Father looked thoroughly taken aback. But I’d wager that the Father from the very first world, once he understood the circumstances, would go along with it too.
“We could go to Siltvelt too, I say.”
“Then that would be best. After all... these are followers of a nation that enslaved the demi-humans of the Seaetto territory. There’s no need for your heart to ache over it.”
The mixed-breed lizardman’s brow furrowed slightly.
“Sion, is this an unpleasant topic?”
Father immediately asked.
“...Why ask me?”
“Because you reacted differently from the others. I was just asking if you knew something about it.”
“Sion, if you stay silent, I can’t learn anything. Say what you want to say—I like to think I’m a generous master.”
Father tried to press the silent mixed-breed lizardman into speaking, his tone growing firmer.
“Do you have complaints about humans trading in slaves?”
“That’s not it. I agree with the proposal... it’s a fitting punishment for people from a nation that hunted slaves amid the chaos of their lord’s death.”
“I see.”
There seemed to be some weight behind those words, I say.
